summary.text: In Mandarin, 的 marks possession or links a modifier to a noun. One analysis treats it as 白 “white” plus sound-bearing 勺. A traditional account analyzes 旳 as 日 plus 勺, glosses it “bright,” and calls 的 its common form; the graphic change is not dated or explained.

formation.text: The main analysis is phonosemantic: 白 contributes a white-related meaning and 勺 supplies a sound cue. A traditional analysis of 旳 assigns brightness-related meaning to 日 and a sound role to 勺; it describes 的 as the common form. The date and process connecting the written forms remain uncertain.

components.text: In the traditional analysis of 旳, 日 contributes brightness-related meaning. This component belongs to 旳, not the current form 的.
In 旳, 勺 is identified as the sound component. 勺 also means “ladle,” but that separate meaning does not make 旳 a spelling for “ladle.”

sound_limitation.text: The available reconstruction compares 勺 with 的, not 旳, so it provides no reading comparison for 勺 and 旳.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang Old Chinese, 勺 is reconstructed as *pljewɢ and 的 as *pleːwɢ. Their similarity motivates the proposed sound role, but does not establish 旳’s reading.

components.text: In one analysis of 的, 白 contributes the category “white.” Its graphic relationship to 日 in the traditional analysis of 旳 is unresolved.
In one analysis of 的, 勺 supplies a sound cue; the precise original pronunciation is uncertain.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang Old Chinese, one reading of 勺 is reconstructed as *pljewɢ and 的 as *pleːwɢ. Their similarity supports a plausible sound relationship; reconstructions from different systems should not be combined.

history.text: The received Shuo Gua text includes 的顙 in a description of a horse. The traditional explanation connects the phrase with 旳, “bright,” or with the brightness of white; the phrase does not date the graph or settle its interpretation.

The traditional account calls 的 the common form of 旳. The selected image shows 旳 as represented in the Shuowen seal-script tradition; it is a modern drawing, not an ancient inscription. The date and process of the graphic change are uncertain.
的 is also recorded with the meaning “target.” This may extend from a brightness-related or white-mark sense, or may belong to a separate root; the relationship and chronology remain unsettled.

The possessive and attributive particle was written 底 before 的 replaced that spelling. One account dates the substitution to a 1238 stele, while a secondary survey reports 底 in use from Wei–Jin through Song. This spelling change does not show that the particle’s meaning developed from “bright.”

uncertainties.text: The traditional analysis of 旳 uses 日, while a separate analysis of 的 uses 白. The date and process connecting these forms, including any continuous graphic sequence, remain uncertain.
The relationship, if any, among the brightness, white-forehead, and target uses is unsettled; no semantic path among them is established.
The particle’s spoken origin is disputed. Proposals connect 底 with 之, 者, or the demonstrative 底; the accounts do not settle among them.

senses.text: A target sense is recorded for 的. It may relate to brightness or a white mark, but a separate lexical root is also proposed; the relationship and chronology are unsettled.

senses.period: Late Middle Chinese onward; precise chronology disputed

limitations.text: The traditional “bright” gloss belongs to 旳; 的顙 does not establish that 的 itself had this sense or date it.
The bright and target senses do not establish a chronological semantic development between them.

evidence.text: Phonosemantic compound. 白 represents the meaning and 勺 represents the sound. The character is based on the original meaning "bright white", which is unrelated to the modern meaning.

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *pleːwɢ): semantic 白 (“white”) + phonetic 勺 (OC *pljewɢ, *bljewɢ).
The original form was 旳 with the meaning of “bright”, hence the initial 日 semantic. See Etymology 1 below.
For the "bright" sense, probably related to 曜 (OC *lewɢs, “to shine; daylight”); see there for more (STEDT).
The sense of “mark in a target” may be secondary. Alternatively, it may be an independent root on its own. Compare Tibetan རྟགས (rtags, “mark, sign”).

First attested in the Tang Dynasty as 底. This glyph was borrowed later to represent de, the possessive marker in Northern Chinese, superseding the earlier 底 as a way to write this word.
There are three main competing proposals for its etymology:
* Derived from the lenition of the literary genitive marker 之 (OC *tjɯ) (Demiéville, 1950; Wang, 1958; Mei, 1988), which is still preserved in many phrases, and in the written form to some extent, especially in Taiwan.
* Derived from the lenition of 者 (OC *tjaːʔ, “nominalizer > medieval possessive”) (Lü, 1943; Yuan et al., 1996; Yang, R., 2016). Note that 的 is also a nominalizer like 者 in Classical Chinese.
* Derived from the lenition of Middle Chinese demonstrative 底 (MC tejX) (Shi, 2015, 2023).
If from either of the first two etymons, possibly cognate with the demonstrative 這／这 (zhè).
Possibly cognate with the particle sense of 地, which is homophonic but now has its specialised usage.
In contemporary times it is also used to represent unrelated equivalent particles in other Chinese varieties. Examples include Hokkien ê (variously also written as 个, 之, 兮, 亓, ㄟ, possibly derived from 其 according to Douglas (1873) although the Arte de la Lengua Chiõ Chiu (1620) and Dictionario Hispanico Sinicum (1626-1642) historically used 个), Eastern Min gì (其), Wu geq (個) and Cantonese ge³ (嘅 < 個).
Phonetic syllable used to transcribe certain syllables in foreign loanwords.

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, online text and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 旳 entry; graphic history and gloss
evidence.text: The Han Shuowen entry records 旳 as “bright,” formed from 日 with 勺 as phonetic, and cites the Yi phrase 爲旳顙. Duan Yucai says 旳 is the brightness of white, that the common form became 的, and that the graph’s sense extended to an archery target. This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of the original graph’s pre-Han history.
evidence.title: 說文解字「旳」— Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Han Dian (ZDIC), 旳 entry quoting Shuowen and Duan Yucai
evidence.text: The entry reproduces Shuowen’s 日 + phonetic 勺 analysis and Duan’s explanation that 旳 means white’s brightness, with 的 as the common form. It cites the Eastern Han Lu Jun stele for a reduplicated 旳旳 use and lists clerical script examples, including the Lu Jun stele and Eastern Han Xiaoguan stele. The page displays script labels and images, but those image glyphs were not independently inspected here.
evidence.title: 旳 dì — 汉典

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, Tsu-lin Mei
evidence.field: Abstract: competing origins and chronology of 底/的 particle
evidence.text: Mei (1988) argues that the particle 底 derives from colloquial 之 rather than 者, describing a sound split in which literary 之 preserves a medial lost in the colloquial form. He rejects a 者 > 底 derivation on phonological grounds and proposes grammatical pathways for the phrase-final nominalizer. He dates the particle 底 to Late Middle Chinese, around the 8th–9th centuries, and reports 的 replacing 底 in a 1238 stele. These are Mei’s arguments, while other published analyses disagree.
evidence.title: The Origin of the Particle ‘.te’ 的 and ‘ti’ 底 — Bulletin of the Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica

evidence.source: Lee Sodong, Korean Citation Index journal article record and abstract
evidence.field: Abstract: development of nominalization markers 所, 者, 之 and 底
evidence.text: The 2015 study describes competing origin accounts for 底 as unresolved while noting that the 者-origin account is the most widely accepted among scholars; its own analysis broadly supports that proposal by tracing how 所, 者, and 之 constructions converged in Tang-period 底 constructions. This directly conflicts with Mei’s 之-origin account and illustrates that the grammatical history remains disputed.
evidence.title: 고대중국어 명사화표지 ‘所’, ‘者’, ‘之’의 통일과정 연구 — KCI record

evidence.source: Qihongtao, Longdong University Journal portal article record and abstract
evidence.field: Abstract and bibliography: early uses of 底 and later spelling substitution
evidence.text: The abstract reports 底 as pronoun and particle in Wei–Jin period literature, widespread in Tang and Five Dynasties texts and still common in Song-period writing; after Yuan, its pronoun use became rare and the particle was replaced by 的. The article is a secondary survey and says its full text must be obtained through CNKI, so the underlying dated examples could not be checked here.
evidence.title: 近代汉语中“底”字的来源及其演变 — 陇东学院学报

evidence.text: The received Shuo Gua text includes “其於馬也，為善鳴、為馵足、為的顙” (for horses: good at neighing, white-footed, and 的顙). This confirms an early textual use in a phrase interpreted by Shuowen and later commentators as describing a white forehead; the received text itself does not date the character form or establish whether this is the same lexical root as the target sense.
evidence.title: 易傳/說卦 — 維基文庫

evidence.text: The page describes 的 as phonosemantic, semantic 白 ‘white’ plus phonetic 勺, and says the earlier written form was 旳 with 日. It displays a small-seal entry for 旳 but no securely attested oracle-bone or bronze forms of 的. Therefore this research supports the received Shuowen distinction between 旳 and common 的, but cannot assert an unbroken paleographic sequence or identify a corruption event between forms.
evidence.title: 的 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese entry 的; reconstructions attributed to Baxter–Sagart (2014) and Zhengzhang (2003)
evidence.field: Old Chinese and Middle Chinese readings for bright/target 的
evidence.text: For the lexical bright/target character, the page gives Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[t-l]ˤewk and Middle Chinese tek, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *pleːwɢ. The distinct systems yield substantially different Old Chinese forms; these are reconstructions rather than direct attestations. Standard Mandarin readings listed for this lexical sense include dì and dí; Cantonese Jyutping is dik1.
evidence.title: 的 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese entry 勺; reconstructions attributed to Baxter–Sagart (2014) and Zhengzhang (2003)
evidence.field: Pronunciation and historical comparisons for proposed sound component 勺
evidence.text: The 勺 entry gives multiple lexical readings: the noun ‘ladle’ has Mandarin sháo, Middle Chinese dzyak and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *m-tewk; a separate verb reading has Mandarin zhuó, Middle Chinese tsyak and Baxter–Sagart *t-ewk. Zhengzhang (2003) lists 勺 *bljewɢ for one reading and *pljewɢ for another. Since 的 is Zhengzhang *pleːwɢ and 勺 has *pljewɢ readings in that same system, the within-system comparison supports 勺 as a plausible phonetic element in 的; reconstruction mismatch across systems prevents claiming the precise original sound. 勺 is also an independently glossed ladle, but the sound-component claim does not require that referent to be the source of a whole-graph loan.
evidence.title: 勺 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese entry 白; reconstructions attributed to Baxter–Sagart (2014) and Zhengzhang (2003)
evidence.field: Pronunciation and history of semantic component 白
evidence.text: The page lists Mandarin bái, Middle Chinese bæk, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *bˤrak, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *braːɡ for 白 ‘white’. Zhengzhang’s reconstruction gives its phonetic-series role, but the page reports competing theories for the graph’s earliest pictorial referent (including an acorn and a human head). This uncertainty about 白’s own graphic origin does not negate its traditional semantic function ‘white’ in the compound analysis.
evidence.title: 白 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese entry 的; section on Etymology 2
evidence.text: The page reports three proposals for the particle’s development: lenition from literary 之, lenition from 者, and grammaticalization of Middle Chinese demonstrative 底 (reconstructed tejX). It states that the proposed 之/者 paths face phonological problems, while Shi’s 底 account treats it as a gradual Tang-period grammaticalization and distinguishes the grammatical functions. It lists Standard Mandarin particle de and dì, Cantonese dik1, plus multiple readings for regional equivalents. This is a secondary compilation rather than direct corpus evidence.
evidence.title: 的 — Wiktionary

evidence.field: Detailed definitions and dated cited examples
evidence.text: The entry separates particle de from lexical dì/dí. It cites the archery-target sense in Xunzi’s Encouraging Learning (“質的張而弓矢至焉”) and Wang Chong’s Lunheng, and cites a ‘bright’ sense in Song Yu’s Shennü Fu (“朱唇的其若丹”). These are source quotations transmitted in later works; no date or manuscript witness for the particular graph spelling was verified here. The gloss list should not be treated as a chronology of semantic change.
evidence.title: 的 de, dī, dí, dì — 汉典

Zhengzhang (2003) lists 勺 *bljewɢ for one reading and *pljewɢ for another. Since 的 is Zhengzhang *pleːwɢ and 勺 has *pljewɢ readings in that same system, the within-system comparison supports 勺 as a plausible phonetic element in 的; reconstruction mismatch across systems prevents claiming the precise original sound. 勺 is also an independently glossed ladle, but the sound-component claim does not require that referent to be the source of a whole-graph loan.
evidence.title: 勺 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese entry 白; reconstructions attributed to Baxter–Sagart (2014) and Zhengzhang (2003)
evidence.field: Pronunciation and history of semantic component 白
evidence.text: The page lists Mandarin bái, Middle Chinese bæk, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *bˤrak, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *braːɡ for 白 ‘white’. Zhengzhang’s reconstruction gives its phonetic-series role, but the page reports competing theories for the graph’s earliest pictorial referent (including an acorn and a human head). This uncertainty about 白’s own graphic origin does not negate its traditional semantic function ‘white’ in the compound analysis.
evidence.title: 白 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese entry 的; section on Etymology 2
evidence.text: The page reports three proposals for the particle’s development: lenition from literary 之, lenition from 者, and grammaticalization of Middle Chinese demonstrative 底 (reconstructed tejX). It states that the proposed 之/者 paths face phonological problems, while Shi’s 底 account treats it as a gradual Tang-period grammaticalization and distinguishes the grammatical functions. It lists Standard Mandarin particle de and dì, Cantonese dik1, plus multiple readings for regional equivalents. This is a secondary compilation rather than direct corpus evidence.
evidence.title: 的 — Wiktionary

evidence.field: Detailed definitions and dated cited examples
evidence.text: The entry separates particle de from lexical dì/dí. It cites the archery-target sense in Xunzi’s Encouraging Learning (“質的張而弓矢至焉”) and Wang Chong’s Lunheng, and cites a ‘bright’ sense in Song Yu’s Shennü Fu (“朱唇的其若丹”). These are source quotations transmitted in later works; no date or manuscript witness for the particular graph spelling was verified here. The gloss list should not be treated as a chronology of semantic change.
evidence.title: 的 de, dī, dí, dì — 汉典

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcription of Shuowen Jiezi and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 旳 entry; definition, components, and commentary
evidence.text: The entry transcribes Xu Shen’s account of 旳 as ‘bright,’ formed from 日 with 勺 as phonetic, and cites the Shuo Gua phrase 爲旳顙. Duan Yucai explains 旳 as the brightness of white, says the common form is 的, and describes an extended target sense. This preserves historical lexicographic claims; it does not independently establish a pre-Han sequence or a corruption event.
evidence.title: 說文解字「旳」 — Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcription of Shuowen Jiezi and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 勺 entry; object gloss and graphic account
evidence.text: The entry presents 勺 as a ladle/dipping vessel and, in Duan’s explanation, as a vessel with a handle and contents. This is evidence for the separately glossed noun and traditional graphic account of 勺, not evidence that a reconstructed pronoun names that vessel or that the entire 勺 graph was borrowed as a loanword in 旳.
evidence.title: 說文解字「勺」 — Shuowen.org

evidence.field: 旳-seal.svg file description, source and license
evidence.text: The Commons page describes this file as a digitally created Shuowen seal-script style rendering of 旳, identifies 日 and 勺 as components in file metadata, and marks the image as public domain. The page names source databases and identifies Richard Sears as a courtesy permission source. This is a modern drawing, not an image of an ancient inscription or artifact.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No directly inspected oracle-bone, bronze, or excavated manuscript form of 的/旳 was located; the inspected script-history material displayed the Shuowen small-seal tradition but did not establish the first attestation or a continuous graphic evolution.

Shuowen’s Han account identifies 旳 as bright and 勺 as phonetic, while Duan Yucai says common 的 was the later form. The intervening date and process by which 日 form 旳 was replaced or regularized as 白 form 的 remain unverified; avoid describing it as proven graphic corruption.

The graph 各 in 的 has no attested original weapon/tool name requiring a whole-graph phonetic-loan hypothesis. 勺’s sound-component role is a separate claim, supported by Shuowen and same-system Zhengzhang comparison; the historical phonetic realization remains reconstruction-dependent.

The relationship between brightness/white-forehead/target senses is only partly explained by Shuowen and its commentary. The target sense may be an extension from the bright/white mark, or an independent lexical root; no evidence inspected here settles the link.

The particle’s spoken-word history and its written graph history are distinct. Wei–Jin-to-Tang 底 attestations are reported by a secondary survey; Mei locates Late Middle Chinese particle development and the first 的-for-底 substitution in 1238. Direct examination of those primary manuscript and stele examples was not available.

Particle origin remains disputed: Mei argues colloquial 之 > 底; a 2015 study favors 者; another account treats demonstrative 底 as the source. The original dataset evidence for each proposal was not independently collated.

Song Yu’s Shennü Fu and Xunzi quotations are lexicon-cited attestations, but their transmitted text dates and graph variants were not independently established here. Do not infer the semantic chronology solely from dictionary entry order.

Wiktionary’s broad phonetic transcription section includes regional readings; it does not verify every regional particle’s independent etymology. Claims about unrelated homophonous particles in other Sinitic varieties remain outside this evidence review.

The proposed image is a modern digital seal-script rendering based on a Shuowen-style form, not an artifact photograph. No actual oracle-bone, bronze, or excavated manuscript image for 的/旳 was established in these searches.
The Commons file page for 的-seal.svg could not be opened; the usable direct file candidate is specifically the 旳 seal-style drawing.
Xiaoxuetang’s 旳 query returned only the general interface in this web session. No exact record page or image for 旳 was verified, so no Xiaoxuetang image is proposed.

Shuowen and Duan’s accounts support a traditional 日 + phonetic 勺 analysis and a later common 的 form; the transition’s date and mechanism remain unverified. The ladle gloss of 勺 does not itself establish any whole-graph sound borrowing.

This invocation independently verified graph formation and image provenance only. It did not independently recheck the competing particle histories, dated attestations, modern readings, or same-system Old Chinese pronunciation comparisons supplied in the repository dossier.
